creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 12, item 1.

A rad block decodes its JSON through float64, so 64-bit IDs and nanosecond timestamps come out rounded with no error. `http_get(...).body` and `parse_json` keep the same values exact, so the answer depends on which fetch path the script used.

```rad
Id = json[].id
rad "http://example.invalid/items":
    fields Id
r = http_get("http://example.invalid/items")
print("http_get:", r.body[0].id)
```

With `--mock-response '.*:big.json'` and `big.json` = `[{"id": 230428225367445504}]`, on main:

```
Id
230428225367445500
http_get: 230428225367445504
```

In the real case the printed ID did not exist when looked up again.

Where: `core/requester.go` `RequestJson` (called from `core/rad_block.go:576`) uses plain `json.Unmarshal`; `core/utils.go:104` already has a `UseNumber` decoder that http_* uses.
title: rad blocks round JSON integers above 2^53
